title: RD-MT166-OrchestrationAuditSurface

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the WP-017 ORCHESTRATION AUDIT SURFACE -- the one operator-facing place that answers 'who spawned / steered / interrupted whom, when, and with what outcome' by joining the Flight Recorder events (MT-161) with the durable PG ledgers (MT-162) into a filterable projection, exposed over an HTTP read route, rendered in a native diagnostics pane (swarm_lane_diagnostics pattern), mirrored in a React read surface, and exportable as a portable evidence bundle. This is the RD family's designated GUI MT: the other RD MTs are headless or read-only-lane extensions and explicitly defer the WP-017 new-operator-pane + Argus obligation to THIS MT.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) new backend projection module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/orchestration_audit.rs building OrchestrationAuditProjection by joining the MT-162 AgentSteeringLedgerStore rows (steer messages, parent-child attribution, MT runs, merge actions) with correlated MT-161 FR events, filterable by session_id / parent_session_id / wp_id / mt_id / merge_id / time-range; (b) module registration in swarm_orchestration/mod.rs; (c) new HTTP route file src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/orchestration_audit.rs (pub fn routes(state: AppState) -> Router following api/flight_recorder.rs: GET query with an AuditFilter extractor + a GET export endpoint returning a portable evidence bundle) + registration in api/mod.rs; (d) native diagnostics pane src/frontend/handshake_native/src/orchestration_audit_diagnostics.rs implementing PaneFactory (PaneType::OrchestrationAudit) with stable author-id helpers, mirroring swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs; (e) React read surface app/src/components/session/OrchestrationAuditPanel.tsx (read-only) + its sibling test; (f) tests: backend join/filter/export tests, native pane projection-validation test, React component test.

DETAILED SPEC -- AUDIT PROJECTION (orchestration_audit.rs): the projection is a JOIN, not a new source of truth. Inputs: AgentSteeringLedgerStore.list_* (MT-162: agent_steer_messages, agent_parent_child_attribution, agent_mt_runs, agent_merge_actions) as the durable spine, correlated to FR events by message_id / merge_id / run ids / session_id / parent_session_id (the correlation block MT-161 stamps on every payload). Output OrchestrationAuditProjection { rows: Vec<AuditRow>, filter_echo, generated_at_unix_ms } where AuditRow captures: actor (who: operator | session_id | role_id), action (spawn/steer/interrupt/resume/notify/mt-dispatch/mt-signal/mt-handoff/merge-*), subject (target session/merge/mt), at_unix_ms, outcome (queued/delivered/acked/rejected/denied/confirmed/executed/conflicted/aborted/...), correlation ids (session_id, parent_session_id, wp_id, mt_id, message_id, merge_id, run_id), and evidence refs (the FR event id + the ledger row key so a row is drillable to its durable source). FILTERS (AuditFilter): session_id, parent_session_id, wp_id, mt_id, merge_id, actor, action, since_unix_ms, until_unix_ms -- these are exactly the list_* filters MT-162 was built to serve; the route echoes the applied filter back so the projection is reproducible. The projection is READ-ONLY: it issues no writes, mutates no ledger, and holds no raw steer TEXT (it shows payload_sha256 + a link to the MT-163 transcript custody surface for full text).

HTTP ROUTE (api/orchestration_audit.rs, api/flight_recorder.rs pattern -- Router::new().route(...).route(...), Query<AuditFilter> extractor, Json responses, AppState): GET /orchestration_audit -> OrchestrationAuditProjection (filtered); GET /orchestration_audit/export -> portable evidence bundle (a self-contained JSON document: schema_id 'hsk.orchestration_audit_bundle@1', filter_echo, generated_at, the audit rows, and the resolved evidence refs, hash-sealed so it can be shared as portable proof WITHOUT a redaction pass because it carries hashes not raw text -- the MT-162 custody split is what makes this safe). Register both under an /orchestration_audit namespace in api/mod.rs. Read-only verbs only (GET); no POST/mutation on this surface.

NATIVE PANE (orchestration_audit_diagnostics.rs, swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs pattern): OrchestrationAuditDiagnosticsPaneFactory implementing PaneFactory with pane_type() -> PaneType::OrchestrationAudit, an offline()/with_projection()/with_transport() constructor set, and STABLE ELEMENT/AUTHOR IDS for parallel-model GUI testing (scoped_author_id + per-row author-id helpers modeled on swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs run_author_id/message_author_id/lane_author_id lines 1070-1141, e.g. audit_row_author_id(row_id), audit_filter_author_id(field)). The pane is READ-ONLY, must not steal focus or pop (HBR-QUIET), and exposes structured state a no-context model can read (Argus-visible). Add PaneType::OrchestrationAudit to the pane registry additively. Provide validate_projection_for_native_surface-style validation (swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs line 1141) so malformed projections cannot render.

REACT SURFACE (app/src/components/session/OrchestrationAuditPanel.tsx, read-only): renders the audit rows as a filterable table (actor -> action -> subject -> outcome -> time) with stable data-testid attributes per row and per filter control, drill-down revealing correlation ids + evidence refs + a link to the transcript (MT-163) for full text, and an Export button that GETs the evidence bundle. NO write/steer/interrupt controls on this panel (interactive steering is the session/steering families' surface). Named allowed exception to the app/src/** freeze; no other app/src file changes beyond the panel + its wiring + test.

ARGUS: the native pane is an Argus target (HBR-VIS): its stable element ids (audit rows, filter controls, export trigger, empty-state) are the argus_targets a parallel model queries to verify the surface renders real joined PG+FR rows -- readable, discoverable, coherent, non-overlapping, responsive, important-state-visible (the GLOBAL-BUILD GUI verification checklist).

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the grounding first: swarm_orchestration/agent_steering_ledger.rs (MT-162: the four stores + list_* filter methods this projection joins), flight_recorder/events_agent_steering.rs (MT-161: FR ids + correlation block) and api/flight_recorder.rs (routes() + Query<EventFilter> + list_events pattern -- the route template), swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs (ModelLaneDiagnosticsProjection precedent), src/frontend/handshake_native/src/swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs IN FULL (SwarmLaneDiagnosticsProjection/PaneFactory/PaneType usage, scoped_author_id line 960, per-entity author-id helpers 1070-1141, validate_projection_for_native_surface 1141, pane_registry PaneType/PaneFactory), src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs (PaneType enum + PaneFactory trait), app/src/components/session/SessionReplayPanel.tsx (React read-surface + data-testid convention), api/mod.rs (route registration).
2. Backend projection: orchestration_audit.rs with AuditRow, AuditFilter, OrchestrationAuditProjection, build_orchestration_audit_projection(ledger, fr_source, filter) joining ledger rows to FR events by the correlation ids; ordered by at_unix_ms; read-only.
3. Evidence bundle: OrchestrationAuditBundle (schema_id hsk.orchestration_audit_bundle@1) + to_bundle(projection) that seals the rows + filter_echo + generated_at with a content hash; carries hashes/evidence refs only (no raw text) so it is shareable without redaction.
4. HTTP route: api/orchestration_audit.rs routes(state) with GET /orchestration_audit (Query<AuditFilter>) and GET /orchestration_audit/export; register in api/mod.rs. Managed-PG-gated tests like MT-162 (HANDSHAKE_TEST_DATABASE_URL present -> run; absent -> typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF skip, never fake PASS).
5. Native pane: orchestration_audit_diagnostics.rs PaneFactory + PaneType::OrchestrationAudit (added to pane_registry additively) + stable author-id helpers + projection validation; non-focus-stealing (HBR-QUIET).
6. React: OrchestrationAuditPanel.tsx read-only table + filters + drill-down + Export, stable data-testid per row/control; sibling component test rendering a fixture projection; assert NO button role that writes/steers.
7. Tests: backend join correctness (a spawn+steer+ack+merge fixture produces the expected AuditRows with correct actor/subject/outcome + evidence refs), filter correctness (each AuditFilter field narrows as expected + filter_echo reproducible), export bundle shape + hash-seal + no-raw-text assertion; native pane projection-validation + stable-id smoke; React component read-only render + testid presence.
8. cargo build -p handshake_core + handshake-native green; clippy clean; React build/tests green for the touched component; Argus render check on the native pane per the crate's GUI-test convention.

acceptance_criteria: orchestration_audit.rs builds an OrchestrationAuditProjection by JOINING MT-162 ledger rows with correlated MT-161 FR events -- read-only, no writes, no ledger mutation, no raw steer text (payload_sha256 + transcript link only).

AuditRow answers who-spawned/steered/interrupted-whom, when, and with what outcome: actor, action, subject, at_unix_ms, outcome, full correlation ids, and evidence refs (FR event id + ledger row key) drillable to the durable source.
AuditFilter supports session_id / parent_session_id / wp_id / mt_id / merge_id / actor / action / since / until, and the route echoes the applied filter so the projection is reproducible.

GET /orchestration_audit returns the filtered projection; GET /orchestration_audit/export returns a portable evidence bundle (schema_id hsk.orchestration_audit_bundle@1) that is hash-sealed and carries hashes/evidence refs only -- shareable without a redaction pass; both registered in api/mod.rs; read-only verbs only.

Native OrchestrationAuditDiagnosticsPaneFactory implements PaneFactory with PaneType::OrchestrationAudit (added additively to the pane registry), stable author-id helpers per row/filter/control, projection validation, and is non-focus-stealing (HBR-QUIET).

React OrchestrationAuditPanel.tsx renders the rows read-only with stable data-testid per row and per filter control, drill-down to correlation ids + evidence refs + transcript link, and an Export action -- NO write/steer/interrupt controls (component test asserts absence of write button roles).

Argus targets (native pane element ids) are named and render real joined PG+FR rows: readable, discoverable, coherent, non-overlapping, responsive, important-state-visible (GLOBAL-BUILD GUI checklist).
PG-backed tests green when managed PostgreSQL is present; typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF skip otherwise -- never fabricated PASS.
cargo build -p handshake_core + handshake-native green; clippy clean; React build/tests green for the touched component.

implementation_notes: This is the RD family's GUI carrier: MT-161/162/164 are headless and MT-163 only extends existing replay surfaces read-only -- all of them defer the WP-017 new-operator-pane + Argus obligation to this MT. Do not add a second audit pane elsewhere.

The projection is a JOIN over existing durable truth (MT-162 ledgers as the spine, MT-161 FR events for correlation) -- it is NOT a new source of truth and must never write. If a join key is missing, that is an MT-161/MT-162 contract bug to surface, not a reason to add a column here.

Portable-evidence-bundle safety rests on the MT-162 custody split: ledgers and FR payloads hold hashes/previews, never raw steer text (full text lives in the MT-163 transcript). Because the bundle carries only hashes + evidence refs, it is shareable as proof without a redaction pass -- assert no-raw-text in the export test.

Follow api/flight_recorder.rs exactly for the route shape (routes(state) -> Router, Query<Filter> extractor, Json) and swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs exactly for the native pane (PaneFactory, PaneType, stable author-id helpers, validate_projection_for_native_surface, non-focus-stealing) -- these are the proven parallel-model-friendly patterns (HBR-SWARM/HBR-VIS/HBR-QUIET).

READ-ONLY is a hard contract line for every surface here: GET-only routes, no PaneFactory write actions, no steer/interrupt buttons in the React panel. Interactive orchestration is owned by the session/steering families; this pane only observes.

Depends on MT-161 (FR ids/correlation) and MT-162 (ledger stores/list_* filters) but NOT MT-163 -- it links to the transcript surface by reference (message_id) rather than depending on the transcript entry types; if MT-163 has not landed, the transcript link degrades to the message_id + sha256 without breaking the audit surface.

surfaces: HTTP: GET /orchestration_audit (filtered projection) + GET /orchestration_audit/export (portable evidence bundle) -- api/orchestration_audit.rs
React: app/src/components/session/OrchestrationAuditPanel.tsx (read-only audit table + filters + drill-down + export)
argus_targets: orchestration-audit.row.* (per audit-row author id via audit_row_author_id)
gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: N/A -- this MT IS the WP-017 operator audit pane: it creates a new operator-facing surface (native pane + React panel + HTTP routes) with named Argus targets, carrying the RD family's GUI + Argus obligation.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: N/A -- a new operator surface ships here, so a UserManual entry (purpose/workflow/routes/filters/export/failure/recovery) is authored in the SAME change per the MT-165 same-change conformance check; add the orchestration-audit page to the MT-165 harness corpus and bump USER_MANUAL_VERSION.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: flight_recorder: WIRED -- the audit projection joins MT-161 FR events as the correlation layer; Tier-1 is the shipped evidence the pane surfaces

internal_diagnostics: typed DEFERRED(reason=WP-KERNEL-015-not-shipped) unless the internal_diagnostics tier exists at implementation time; disposition recorded by MT-164 (the audit pane MAY add an internal_diagnostics column that renders DEFERRED per the MT-164 manifest)
palmistry: typed DEFERRED(reason=WP-KERNEL-015-not-shipped) unless Palmistry exists at implementation time; disposition recorded by MT-164
risk_if_missed: No operator can answer who-spawned/steered/interrupted-whom: the MT-161 FR events and MT-162 ledger rows exist but are never joined into an inspectable, filterable, exportable surface; orchestration disputes are unauditable, the RD family ships no GUI + no Argus coverage, and there is no portable evidence bundle to share as proof.

risks: RISK-1: Write creep -- the audit projection or pane grows a 'convenient' write/steer/resend action, creating an unowned orchestration write path that bypasses the session family's queue/ledger discipline.
RISK-2: Evidence-bundle leak -- the export bundle embeds raw steer text (secrets/injection content per MT-104) instead of hashes, turning every shared bundle into a leak surface.
RISK-3: Join fabrication -- missing correlation ids are papered over with guessed/fuzzy joins, so the audit shows a who-steered-whom relationship that the durable rows do not actually support.

RISK-4: UI incoherence -- the native pane pops/steals focus during parallel-model runs, lacks stable ids, or renders overlapping/unreadable rows, failing the GLOBAL-BUILD GUI checklist and Argus verification.

RISK-5: Filter/pagination lie -- the export or count reflects only the currently loaded/visible subset rather than the full filtered canonical set, so an operator exports partial evidence believing it is complete.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): every surface is GET-only/read-only; component test asserts absence of write button roles in the panel; the pane exposes no write action; contract names the session/steering families as the owners of interactive orchestration.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): the projection and bundle carry payload_sha256 + evidence refs only (never raw text); the export test feeds a marker string through a fixture and asserts it never appears in the bundle -- full text is reachable only via the MT-163 transcript custody surface.

CTRL-3 (RISK-3): joins use only the exact correlation keys MT-161 stamps and MT-162 stores (message_id/merge_id/run_id/session_id/parent_session_id); a row with no durable correlation is shown as such (unjoined) rather than fabricated -- proven by a fixture with a deliberately dangling id.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): the native pane follows swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs (stable author-id helpers, validate_projection_for_native_surface, non-focus-stealing HBR-QUIET); Argus targets are named and verified for readable/discoverable/coherent/non-overlapping/responsive/state-visible.

CTRL-5 (RISK-5): the projection/export operate on the full filtered canonical ledger set (MT-162 list_* over PG), never a UI-rendered subset; filter_echo makes the applied filter explicit and the export test asserts row count equals the canonical filtered count, not the rendered page.

research_provenance.source: Grounded in wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1: api/flight_recorder.rs (routes(state) -> Router with .route('/flight_recorder', get(list_events)) + Query<EventFilter> extractor + Json, lines 71-183 -- the read-route template), src/frontend/handshake_native/src/swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs (SwarmLaneDiagnosticsProjection/PaneFactory/PaneType::SwarmLaneDiagnostics, offline/with_projection/with_transport constructors lines 313-397, scoped_author_id line 960, per-entity author-id helpers run_author_id/message_author_id/lane_author_id lines 1070-1141, validate_projection_for_native_surface line 1141), src/frontend/handshake_native/src/pane_registry.rs (PaneType + PaneFactory trait), swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs (ModelLaneDiagnosticsProjection precedent), app/src/components/session/SessionReplayPanel.tsx (React read-surface + data-testid convention), MT-161 contract (FR ids + correlation block), MT-162 contract (AgentSteeringLedgerStore + list_* filters this projection joins).
corrections: Verified api/flight_recorder.rs uses pub fn routes(state: AppState) -> Router with a Query<EventFilter> extractor and Json responses -- the audit route mirrors it (Query<AuditFilter>, GET-only) rather than inventing a new HTTP style.

Confirmed swarm_lane_diagnostics.rs is a PaneFactory pane (PaneType::SwarmLaneDiagnostics) with stable per-entity author-id helpers (1070-1141) and validate_projection_for_native_surface (1141) -- the audit pane follows this exact parallel-model-friendly, non-focus-stealing pattern and adds PaneType::OrchestrationAudit additively.

Anchored the portable-evidence-bundle safety on the MT-162 custody split (ledgers hold payload_sha256, not raw text; full text is the MT-163 transcript surface), so the export is shareable without a redaction pass -- the export test asserts no raw marker text leaks into the bundle.

Scoped dependencies to MT-161 + MT-162 (FR ids + ledger stores) and made the MT-163 transcript link a by-reference degrade-gracefully feature, so the audit surface does not hard-block on the transcript MT landing first.
